# survival::lung: the NCCTG advanced lung cancer trial (Loprinzi et al. 1994).
main <- function(ctx) {
  d <- survival::lung
  d$event <- as.integer(d$status == 2)  # status: 1 censored, 2 dead
  d$female <- as.integer(d$sex == 2)    # sex: 1 male, 2 female
  file <- file.path(ctx$output_directory, "lung.csv")
  write.csv(d, file, row.names = FALSE)
  ctx$output("lung", list(value = file))

  meaning <- c(time = "Days to death or censoring", event = "death 1 / censored 0", age = "Age", female = "woman 1 / man 0",
               ph.ecog = "ECOG performance status (physician's rating, 0–3)", ph.karno = "Karnofsky score (physician's rating)",
               pat.karno = "Karnofsky score (patient's rating)", meal.cal = "Calories per meal", wt.loss = "Weight loss in the last 6 months (pounds)")
  rows <- lapply(names(meaning), function(v) data.frame(
    Variable = v, Meaning = meaning[[v]], Median = format(median(d[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    Range = sprintf("%g–%g", min(d[[v]], na.rm = TRUE), max(d[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)), Missing = as.character(sum(is.na(d[[v]])))))
  message(nrow(d), " patients, ", sum(d$event), " deaths, survival ", packageVersion("survival"))
  ctx$display_table(do.call(rbind, rows))
}

# Who is included: an age range and a limit on the ECOG performance score.
main <- function(ctx) {
  p <- ctx$params
  d <- read.csv(ctx$path("lung"))
  keep <- d$age >= p$age_min & d$age <= p$age_max
  if (p$ecog_max < 3) keep <- keep & !is.na(d$ph.ecog) & d$ph.ecog <= p$ecog_max
  chosen <- d[keep, ]
  if (sum(chosen$event) < 5) stop("too few deaths in this cohort: ", sum(chosen$event))
  file <- file.path(ctx$output_directory, "cohort.csv")
  write.csv(chosen, file, row.names = FALSE)
  ctx$output("cohort", list(value = file))
  ctx$display_table(data.frame(
    Subjects = c("All 228", sprintf("Aged %d–%d, ECOG %d or less", p$age_min, p$age_max, p$ecog_max)),
    People = c(nrow(d), nrow(chosen)), Deaths = c(sum(d$event), sum(chosen$event)), Women = c(sum(d$female), sum(chosen$female))))
}

library(survival)
library(ggplot2)

# Kaplan-Meier curves by a grouping variable, with the log-rank test.
main <- function(ctx) {
  by <- ctx$params$group
  d <- read.csv(ctx$path("cohort"))
  d$group <- switch(by,
    sex = ifelse(d$female == 1, "Women", "Men"),
    ecog = ifelse(is.na(d$ph.ecog), NA, paste0("ECOG ", pmin(d$ph.ecog, 2), ifelse(d$ph.ecog >= 2, "+", ""))),
    age = ifelse(d$age >= 65, "65 and over", "under 65"),
    stop("group must be sex, ecog or age, not ", by))
  d <- d[!is.na(d$group), ]
  fit <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ group, d)
  test <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ group, d)
  p <- pchisq(test$chisq, length(test$n) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)

  s <- summary(fit, censored = TRUE)
  curves <- data.frame(group = sub("group=", "", s$strata), time = s$time, at_risk = s$n.risk, deaths = s$n.event,
                       censored = s$n.censor, survival = s$surv, lower = s$lower, upper = s$upper)
  table <- summary(fit)$table
  medians <- data.frame(group = sub("group=", "", rownames(table)), n = table[, "records"], deaths = table[, "events"],
                        median = table[, "median"], lower = table[, "0.95LCL"], upper = table[, "0.95UCL"],
                        logrank_chisq = test$chisq, logrank_p = p)
  out <- file.path(ctx$output_directory, "km")
  dir.create(out)
  write.csv(curves, file.path(out, "curves.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(medians, file.path(out, "medians.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  ctx$output("km", list(value = out))

  labels <- setNames(sprintf("%s  n=%d  median %s days", medians$group, medians$n,
                             ifelse(is.na(medians$median), "not reached", sprintf("%.0f", medians$median))), medians$group)
  start <- data.frame(group = medians$group, time = 0, survival = 1, lower = 1, upper = 1)
  line <- rbind(start, curves[, names(start)])
  figure <- ggplot(line, aes(time, survival, colour = group, fill = group)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = curves[curves$censored > 0, ], shape = 3, size = 1.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"), labels = labels, name = NULL, aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Days", y = "Proportion surviving",
         title = sprintf("Kaplan–Meier, log-rank χ² = %.2f, p = %.2g", test$chisq, p),
         subtitle = "Bands are 95% confidence intervals, + marks censoring") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.98), legend.justification = c(1, 1),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  ctx$plot(print(figure), alt = sprintf("Kaplan-Meier curves by %s, log-rank chi-square %.2f", by, test$chisq), width = 7.5, height = 5)
}

library(survival)

# A Cox model on the chosen cohort with the covariates in the param.
main <- function(ctx) {
  covariates <- ctx$params$covariates
  d <- read.csv(ctx$path("cohort"))
  formula <- as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", paste(covariates, collapse = " + ")), env = globalenv())
  fit <- coxph(formula, d, x = TRUE, y = TRUE, model = TRUE)
  s <- summary(fit)
  rows <- data.frame(term = rownames(s$coefficients), coef = s$coefficients[, "coef"], se = s$coefficients[, "se(coef)"],
                     hr = s$conf.int[, "exp(coef)"], lower = s$conf.int[, "lower .95"], upper = s$conf.int[, "upper .95"],
                     p = s$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], n = fit$n, events = fit$nevent)
  out <- file.path(ctx$output_directory, "cox")
  dir.create(out)
  saveRDS(fit, file.path(out, "fit.rds"))
  write.csv(rows, file.path(out, "coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  ctx$output("fit", list(value = out))
  ctx$display_table(data.frame(
    Term = rows$term, HR = sprintf("%.3f", rows$hr), `95%CI` = sprintf("%.3f–%.3f", rows$lower, rows$upper),
    p = sprintf("%.2g", rows$p), n = rows$n, Deaths = rows$events, check.names = FALSE))
}

files.text:
library(survival)
library(ggplot2)

# The same hazard ratio under every combination of who is included and what is adjusted for.
main <- function(ctx) {
  subsets <- ctx$params$subsets
  adjustments <- ctx$params$adjustments
  exposure <- ctx$params$exposure
  d <- read.csv(ctx$path("lung"))

  one <- function(subset_text, adjustment) {
    x <- subset(d, eval(parse(text = subset_text)))
    right <- paste(c(exposure, if (nzchar(adjustment)) adjustment), collapse = " + ")
    fit <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", right)), x)
    s <- summary(fit)
    data.frame(subset = subset_text, adjustment = if (nzchar(adjustment)) adjustment else "no adjustment", n = fit$n, events = fit$nevent,
               hr = s$conf.int[exposure, "exp(coef)"], lower = s$conf.int[exposure, "lower .95"], upper = s$conf.int[exposure, "upper .95"])
  }
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(subsets, function(s) do.call(rbind, lapply(adjustments, function(a) one(s, a)))))
  file <- file.path(ctx$output_directory, "specifications.csv")
  write.csv(rows, file, row.names = FALSE)
  ctx$output("specifications", list(value = file))

  rows$subset <- factor(ifelse(rows$subset == "TRUE", "everyone", rows$subset), levels = ifelse(subsets == "TRUE", "everyone", subsets))
  labelled <- ifelse(adjustments == "", "no adjustment", adjustments)
  rows$adjustment <- factor(rows$adjustment, levels = rev(labelled))
  rows$text <- sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)  n=%d", rows$hr, rows$lower, rows$upper, rows$n)
  right_edge <- max(rows$upper) * 2.4
  figure <- ggplot(rows, aes(hr, adjustment)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0, orientation = "y", colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(x = right_edge, label = text), hjust = 1, size = 3.1, colour = "grey20") +
    facet_grid(subset ~ ., switch = "y") +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.2, 0.5, 1, 2)) +
    labs(x = paste0("Hazard ratio of ", exposure, " (log axis; lines are 95% confidence intervals)"), y = NULL,
         title = "How the hazard ratio moves with whom you include and what you adjust for") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.spacing.y = unit(6, "pt"))
  ctx$plot(print(figure), alt = "Hazard ratio across specifications", width = 8.5, height = 1 + 0.27 * nrow(rows) + 0.1 * length(subsets))
}

notes.html:
Survival analysis: the result moves with "whom" and "what"

The data is lung, bundled with the survival package: real data on 228 patients with advanced lung cancer from the North Central Cancer Treatment Group (NCCTG) (Loprinzi et al., J Clin Oncol 1994;12:601–607).

Survival with censoring is estimated by Kaplan–Meier, and hazard ratios come from a Cox model.

S^(t)=∏ti≤t(1−dini),h(t∣x)=h0(t) eβx\hat S(t)=\prod_{t_i\le t}\Bigl(1-\frac{d_i}{n_i}\Bigr),\qquad h(t\mid x)=h_0(t)\,e^{\beta x}

Change age and ECOG of cohort, covariates of cox, and subsets and adjustments of specs, and rerun just that Card. The figure of specs lays out how far the answer to the same question moves with the specification. Each row of a subgroup has a different number of people, and people missing an adjustment variable drop out.

zph checks proportional hazards. Add ph.karno to covariates to see the assumption become doubtful.

These are associations in old trial data; they show no cause and are not advice on treatment or prognosis.
